## Natural history notes

A large leaf-footed bug characterized by its elongated brown body, long antennae, flattened expansions on the hind legs, and sturdy, somewhat swollen body shape. In Florida, it is found in warm open or semi-open habitats such as scrub edges, pine flatwoods, fields, roadsides, gardens, and woodland margins where shrubs or woody host plants occur. It feeds by piercing plant tissues and sucking sap from stems, fruits, seeds, or new growth, while also serving as prey for birds, spiders, assassin bugs, and other insect-eating animals.
